title: Switch from ⁠text primary key to UUIDv7
body:
Currently, our tables use `text`-based primary keys. This change proposes switching to UUIDv7 for improved performance and consistency.

### db/schema.ts

Before

```ts
export const earlyAccess = createTable('early_access', {
  id: text().primaryKey(),
  email: text().notNull().unique(),
  createdAt: timestamp().notNull(),
  updatedAt: timestamp().notNull(),
});
```

After

```ts
export const earlyAccess = createTable('early_access', {
  id: uuid().primaryKey().$defaultFn(uuidv7),
  email: text().notNull().unique(),
  createdAt: timestamp().notNull(),
  updatedAt: timestamp().notNull(),
});
```

---

### apps/mail/app/api/auth/early-access/route.ts

Before

```ts
const result = await db.insert(earlyAccess).values({
  id: crypto.randomUUID(),
  email,
  createdAt: nowDate,
  updatedAt: nowDate,
});
```

After

```ts apps/mail/app/api/auth/early-access/route.ts
const result = await db.insert(earlyAccess).values({
  email,
  createdAt: nowDate,
  updatedAt: nowDate,
});
```

**Implementation Plan**

1. Identify all tables currently using text primary keys
2. Create migration scripts to convert existing tables
3. Update related code to handle the new UUID format

I'm not sure about google auth. If I login to your service with google auth I'd assume it syncs up my emails to the inbox. If this is on-premise, it shouldn't rely on an email provider and should have it's own users, domains, access roles and everything in between. Then we could allow a user to 
1. Connect a gmail/outlook inbox
